title: Larkspur Insurance - control handoff and trust portal orientation
summary: Introductory posture review focusing on SOC 2 / ISO 27001 artifacts, Trust Center access model, RBAC/SSO patterns, audit log retention and KMS flows. SE demo of where reports live; discussed data residency constraints for EU customers and mapping of Larkspur controls to Redwood controls. Agreed next steps: provide Type II report link, create read-only Trust Center user, and a control-mapping table deliverable.
topics: SOC 2 Type II reports and evidence locations
Trust Center read-only accounts and delegation
RBAC model and SSO / SAML setup
Audit logs, retention and export formats
Data residency (EU region) and export controls
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can go ahead and get started. We'll do quick intros then jump into the trust portal and the SOC 2 docs.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Hi, I'm Priya, Head of Security at Larkspur. We've got a tight ISO 27001 appraisal coming up so we're trying to line up evidence paths.
[00:28] Liam O'Neill: Liam, Redwood SE here, I'll walk through where the reports live and the RBAC patterns. Sorry if the audio is a bit, uh, bouncy on my side.
[00:36] Evan Ramirez: Evan from Cloud Infra, we'll be owning the VPC and peering bits. Quick note - Larkspur has EU customers so residency is a big deal for us.
[00:44] Sara Holt: And I'm Sara, compliance - we'll need the control mappings and timelines.
[00:48] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[00:52] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda: 1) show Trust Center, 2) SOC 2/ISO artifacts, 3) RBAC/SSO patterns and KMS, 4) next steps. Liam, can you share the portal?
[01:05] Liam O'Neill: Yep, sharing now. So on the Trust Center we have the SOC 2 Type II PDF and a separate evidence package link - it's a zipped bundle with test results and syslogs. Note that for some customers we redact sensitive snippets; for enterprise packages you can request the full artifact under NDA.
[01:30] Priya Nair: Is the evidence bundle timestamped with log retention windows? We need to show change history for, like, 12 months.
[01:38] Liam O'Neill: Yes, logs in the bundle are stamped. Our default retention for audit logs is 180 days on hosted tier, but for Dedicated or Private you can extend. We can export to your S3 bucket for longer retention; the export is JSONL and gzipped.
[01:56] Tom Wu: When you say Dedicated, do you mean Reserved GPU pools or the VPC-hosted? We're planning to co-locate some inference in our eu-west-1 region.
[02:06] Maya Chen: Dedicated is the reserved capacity product, you can pin region. For strict residency you may want Redwood Private which gives you a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC. But that has operational tradeoffs, Liam can cover those.
[02:20] Liam O'Neill: Right. Private gives you a private control plane and you manage your KMS key material if needed. For KMS we integrate with AWS KMS and bring-your-own key (BYOK) workflows; key rotation is supported through the KMS lifecycle. Small caveat: if you use Redwood-managed keys there are audit logs on our side for key usage; for BYOK key usage only shows that Redwood called that key but not the raw key material.
[02:48] Priya Nair: Ok, we want BYOK for EU data. Also we need to know how RBAC maps to our internal roles - who can see PII in prompt traces, can you mask that?
[02:58] Liam O'Neill: We have role-scoped permissions in the Trust Center: admin, auditor, viewer. Viewer access can be restricted to metadata-only; full auditor role sees full traces. We also have a masking pipeline that truncates or redacts tokens flagged by a regex or our PII classifier - it's configurable per-tenant.
[03:20] Evan Ramirez: Is SSO SAML 2.0 supported? We will put in a SAML connection through Okta.
[03:26] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML SSO is supported, and SSO provisioning supports SCIM for group sync. We recommend using group-based RBAC so you centralize role changes in Okta.
[03:35] Sara Holt: For ISO 27001 we'll need evidence of provisioning changes - is there an audit trail for SCIM syncs and role changes?
[03:42] Liam O'Neill: Absolutely. All identity events are in the audit log: SCIM provisioning events, SAML assertions, role changes. They are exported as structured events with actor, timestamp, and object. Small note: sometimes the assertion nameID is truncated in transcription, so check the raw event if needed.
[04:00] Maya Chen: Quick demo: clicking into SOC 2 report. This is the Type II for 2024-10 to 2025-04 performed by NorthBridge Assurance. The SOC PDF includes control test matrices; the evidence bundle links to specific test artifacts.
[04:20] Priya Nair: Who's the auditor? NorthBridge, I think I've seen them. We use KPMG for some controls so we'll want to cross-walk those.
[04:28] Liam O'Neill: NorthBridge did the Redwood Type II. If you need crosswalks to particular frameworks (ISO 27001, PCI) we can export a mapping sheet - it's auto-generated but may need manual review.
[04:45] Tom Wu: On the logs export, you said JSONL - does it include the KV cache keys or truncated? We need to prove non-reproducibility.
[04:55] Liam O'Neill: We purposely redact the KV cache values, you get the metadata (cache hit/miss and key id) but not the raw cached token. That aligns with our non-reproducibility guidance.
[05:09] Speaker 6: (crosstalk)
[05:12] Maya Chen: Moving on to control mapping. Sara, what format do you prefer? CSV, spreadsheet, or a columnar matrix?
[05:19] Sara Holt: Spreadsheet with columns: Larkspur control ID, Redwood control, evidence location, owner, frequency. Then a pass/fail column for the auditor.
[05:27] Maya Chen: Great. We'll produce that. Liam, can you confirm who at Redwood will own the evidence handoff?
[05:33] Liam O'Neill: I'll be the SE point, and Maya will own commercial/provisioning. For the actual artifacts, our trust team owns the repository but we can create a read-only Trust Center account for Sara and Priya to review.
[05:46] Priya Nair: Read-only is fine but we need to restrict it to metadata-only for most of our staff; only me and the auditor should have full evidence view.
[05:54] Liam O'Neill: Noted. We can set granular team roles in the Trust Center.
[06:00] Tom Wu: A question on key rotation: if we rotate keys monthly in KMS, how do you handle session tokens with cached model states?
[06:09] Liam O'Neill: Good question. Redwood's runtime caches model KV data in memory for latency; keys are used at rest for model artifacts and stored secrets. When you rotate KMS keys we rewrap secrets and keep the runtime using in-memory caches unaffected; for long-lived sessions we have a reconciliation job that re-encrypts persisted artifacts. It's a bit technical but we can send the KMS flow diagram.
[06:30] Maya Chen: We'll attach that diagram.
[06:32] Priya Nair: About data residency - we need contract language that guarantees no token routing outside eu-west-1. Is that available for Private or Dedicated?
[06:41] Maya Chen: Private is the strictest - you control the control plane and networking. For Dedicated, we can pin nodes to region and route requests within that region but some control plane metadata may cross regions unless you choose Private. We'll share the residency appendix language.
[06:58] Evan Ramirez: And what about backups and logs - do you replicate to us or to Redwood-managed S3?
[07:05] Liam O'Neill: For Private we can configure your own S3 bucket in your account for all artifacts; for Dedicated we typically store in Redwood-managed buckets but can set up cross-account replication on request.
[07:18] Sara Holt: Any SOC 2 exceptions or open findings in the last report?
[07:23] Liam O'Neill: There were two low-risk findings around monitoring thresholds and a remediation plan; both resolved. The Type II opinion was unqualified.
[07:32] Priya Nair: Good. We'll need copies with redaction of customer-identifiable data for auditor sharing.
[07:38] Maya Chen: We'll do that.
[07:40] Liam O'Neill: Quick demo - showing the audit log export UI, you can filter by event types: auth, key-usage, model-call, provisioning. You can set retention policy and schedule exports.
[07:54] Tom Wu: For scheduled exports does it support streaming to our SIEM via syslog or only S3 delivery?
[08:01] Liam O'Neill: Right now S3 delivery is standard; we have a SIEM connector in beta that streams via syslog/HTTP event collector. We can add you to beta if needed.
[08:12] Priya Nair: We'd like that beta.
[08:15] Maya Chen: Noted. I'll add that to next steps.
[08:18] Speaker 6: (quiet)
[08:22] Liam O'Neill: Back to RBAC: we also support attribute-based access, so you can do fine-grained policies like role+tag. Example: allow auditor role read access only for traces that are tagged production but not pii.
[08:36] Sara Holt: How are tags applied to traces? Is there auto-tagging?
[08:40] Liam O'Neill: There's a combination: client-side metadata tags, plus server-side classification. We surfaced a small console to review tags and re-classify. Occasionally the classifier mislabels some things — there's a manual override.
[08:55] Maya Chen: We should call out a known limitation: for hosted customers, certain metadata (like per-token debug IDs) may be aggregated in control plane logs that are out of region unless on Private. Not a blocker but something to escalate to legal if you need strict contract language.
[09:14] Priya Nair: Understood. Please share the exact clause language for the residency appendix.
[09:20] Maya Chen: Will do.
[09:22] Liam O'Neill: Now the control mapping example - I'm opening a template. It maps Redwood controls to common SOC 2 categories, then to ISO 27001 Annex A references. We'll produce one pre-populated for Larkspur with evidence links.
[09:40] Tom Wu: Timeline question — we have an internal audit starting 2025-11-15. Can we get control mapping and Trust Center read-only access by 2025-10-10?
[09:49] Maya Chen: That's feasible. We'll aim for readiness early October.
[09:52] Priya Nair: Are there any costs for the Trust Center read-only accounts or exporting logs?
[09:58] Maya Chen: Read-only accounts are included in enterprise plans. Long-term log retention exports or Private deployments have associated costs; we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[10:09] Sara Holt: For the ISO 27001 scope, we'll need to show continuity for change management. Do you expose code-deploy or change logs for runtime?
[10:17] Liam O'Neill: We export deployment events (build id, artifacts, deploy time) and change approvals where applicable. For Private we can provide more granular logs.
[10:26] Speaker 6: (mutter)
[10:28] Maya Chen: Ok, nearing the end — let's recap and list clear action items.
[10:33] Liam O'Neill: I'll capture the action items in a follow-up email but verbally: 1) Send SOC 2 Type II redacted PDF and evidence bundle link. 2) Provide Trust Center read-only setup for Priya and Sara. 3) Share KMS flow diagram and BYOK process. 4) Produce a control-mapping spreadsheet pre-populated for Larkspur. 5) Add Larkspur to SIEM streaming beta. 6) Share residency appendix language and sample contract clause.
[10:58] Priya Nair: And I'll send the list of in-scope systems and auditors contact details by next week.
[11:06] Maya Chen: Great. Any last quick Qs?
[11:09] Evan Ramirez: One more—do you have SLA metrics for audit log delivery for exports?
[11:14] Liam O'Neill: Exports are async; typical delivery within 15 minutes for small jobs, can be longer for large bundles. In Dedicated/Private we can provide tighter SLOs. We'll include numbers in the doc.
[11:28] Sara Holt: Thanks everyone.
[11:30] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the spreadsheet.
[11:35] (meeting ends)
